title: Move the table layout out of Customer

task.text: `Customer` knows the shape of its table row. Make the mapper own that knowledge.
`Customer` has `fromRow` and `toRow`, so every schema change edits the domain class. Move the conversion into `CustomerMapper`, keeping its constructor, `find(long)` and `save(Customer)`.

items: `Customer` must no longer mention `Row` or its columns.
Behaviour stays: `save` stores the email lower-cased, and `find` throws `IllegalArgumentException` for a corrupt row.

checks.title: find turns a row into a Customer
An unknown id gives an empty Optional
save updates and lowercases the address
A row with a bad email is rejected
Customer's API has no Row in it

hints.text: Who should know that the table has an `emailAddr` column? Not the domain object. The thing between domain and table needs to be a separate class that owns that translation.
Delete `fromRow` and `toRow` from `Customer`. Give `CustomerMapper` two private methods, one per direction, and call them from `find` and `save`. The lower-casing moves with `toRow`.
